cards.text: Joseph, a slave in Egypt, is locked up in the prison where the king's prisoners are kept (Genesis 39:1, 20). Some time later, two officers offend their master, Pharaoh, the king of Egypt: his chief cupbearer and his chief baker. Pharaoh is angry with them both, and friend, a BAKER in trouble with the boss has me sweating under this hat.

cards.question: Pharaoh locks up his chief cupbearer and chief baker in the same prison where Joseph is confined.
In the prison, the captain of the guard assigns the cupbearer and the baker a personal attendant. Who is it?

cards.text: After they've been in custody for some time, both men have a dream on the same night, and each dream has its own meaning. Friend, I dream about dough chasing me around the bakery, and the only meaning is I sampled too many crumbs before bed.
The next morning, Joseph comes in to see them. He takes one look at those two.

cards.question: When Joseph comes to the cupbearer and the baker in the morning, he sees that they are ___.

cards.text: So Joseph asks them, “Why are your faces so downcast today?” He's locked up himself and he's STILL checking on other people, and friend, I know that move, because I did it for every scared newcomer who slid into the junk drawer I was stuck in for years.

cards.question: Joseph asks the cupbearer and the baker why their faces are so downcast. They tell him they both had dreams. What's the trouble?
Joseph answers the cupbearer and the baker with a question: don't interpretations belong to ___? Then he asks them to tell him their dreams.

cards.text: The chief cupbearer goes first. In his dream there's a vine in front of him with three branches, and as it buds, the blossoms open and the clusters ripen into grapes.

cards.question: In the cupbearer's dream, the grapes are ripe and Pharaoh's cup is in his hand. What does he do next?

answers.text: Squeezes the grapes into it for Pharaoh
Pours the cup out on the ground

cards.text: Joseph replies, “This is the interpretation: The three branches are three days.” Friend, you hand ME a dream and I need a week, two batches and a nap.

cards.question: The three branches are three days. What does Joseph say Pharaoh will do for the cupbearer within three days?

answers.text: Give him a seat on his council
Put him in charge of the prison

cards.text: Then Joseph asks for something. When it goes well for the cupbearer, Joseph asks him to remember him, show him kindness and mention him to Pharaoh, so Pharaoh might bring Joseph out of this prison.
Then Joseph tells the cupbearer how he got to Egypt in the first place: he was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews.

cards.question: Joseph tells the cupbearer he did something to deserve being put in this dungeon.

cards.text: When the chief baker sees that the cupbearer's interpretation was favorable, he speaks up: he had a dream too. Friend, that's like watching a coworker ask the boss for a day off, and the second the boss says yes, you're RIGHT behind him with your own request.

cards.question: In the chief baker's dream, there are ___ baskets of white bread on his head.
In the chief baker's dream, the top basket holds all sorts of baked goods for Pharaoh. What is happening to them?

answers.text: Birds are eating them out of the basket
They are tumbling down to the ground
Servants are carrying them all away

cards.text: Joseph starts the same way: “This is the interpretation: The three baskets are three days.” I bet the baker is holding his breath.

cards.question: The interpretation Joseph gives the chief baker is favorable, just like the cupbearer's.

cards.text: Joseph says that within three days Pharaoh will lift off the baker's head and hang him on a tree, and the birds will eat his flesh. Heavy news, friend.

cards.question: On the third day, Pharaoh holds a feast for all his officials. What's the occasion?

cards.text: And right there, in front of all his officials, Pharaoh lifts up the heads of the chief cupbearer and the chief baker. He restores the cupbearer to his position, and once again the cupbearer places the cup in Pharaoh's hand.
But Pharaoh hangs the chief baker.

cards.question: The chief baker's end comes just as Joseph described in his interpretation.
Joseph asked the chief cupbearer to remember him and mention him to Pharaoh. Now the cupbearer is back serving Pharaoh. What does he do about Joseph?

answers.text: He sends for Joseph right away

cards.text: Forgotten, friend, and I know that one from my years in the back of a junk drawer. We're pulling this batch out of the oven for now, but Joseph's story still has plenty more baking.
